notes.title: 🔩 Sunday Devlog 52: Heavy Framework
notes.content: [p]Good evening.. morning.. what is time anymore??[/p][p][/p][h2]Construction[/h2][p]This week, there's nothing brand new that's [i]complete..[/i] but a bunch of stuff is partially mostly there! The editor, yet again, continues to take shape, and it's been looking pretty good, I think![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/22b4024db628eb9aca0a2cf09b0ad8f4c2ab1ea0.gif"][/img][/p][p]The editor is going to have the background that you upload yourself [i](or pick from presets)[/i] here. This performs a couple of functions; for one, it makes the editor much more visually interesting and immersive, but more importantly it also gives you a reference for how the background will look in-game. A lot of these assets look kind of dull in Aseprite, but that actually is necessary in order to create the low-contrast colors you see in the background. Or you could try more vibrant colors! Whatever you choose to do, this system will give you an instant preview of what your background will look like.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/afbf5531c4ca4b6a213fb132d2a72e7edf735142.gif"][/img][/p][p]In addition, a menu for the editor is in the works! This will consist of a couple standard options buttons [i][b](button positions not final at all!!!) [/b][/i]and on the other side, customization, saving and other options for the editor. Truthfully, I don't know if this is going to be enough space for everything, that's going to fit here, but it should???? be fine, lol.[/p][p][/p][h2]Up next..[/h2][p]Last week I mentioned adding more UI for BPM, offset, title etc adjustments. I was going to do that this week, but became more enamored with the idea of bringing the ingame background into the editor. I think it was worth it, but now I'll actually be getting those config options done lol. Thanks for following the devlogs! :)[/p][p][/p][p][i]-Encabulated Games[/i][/p]

notes.title: ▶ Sunday Devlog 51: FastPlay
notes.content: [p]Welcome back![/p][p][/p][p]I had a heck of a move-in back to college, but now we're back with a new devlog, and I've got some exciting tech to show today:[/p][p][/p][h2]Live Playback![/h2][p]Playing a level in the editor now causes music to play where appropriate, and as a bonus, the parser moves around and is accompanies by some simplified effects + sounds to simulate playing the level!! Be sure to play this one with audio on![/p][previewyoutube="ejA13jYCMuY;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]There were some issues with the old playback system where it would go out of sync, but this one (still using ease) relies on a timer to keep the player in check, even if there are lagspikes. The whole thing is also compatible with any BPM which is a huge relief to be done with as well![/p][p][/p][p]At this point, thanks to this feature, the editor is pretty much capable of being used to map songs if you're a dev with access. A lot still needs to be manually changed, but now for the first time, as long as you plug a lot in, you can effectively have a mapping session :) Yippie!!![/p][p][/p][h2]Next week..[/h2][p]Stuff™ is occurring this week for me as always, but I should be able to get more done on the editor. Now that the player is effectively done, we can move on to actual UI pieces for adjusting BPM, offset, title, and more. I can't wait to talk about it! And now, I'm going to lose a little sleep mapping some of my favorite songs on this thing lol.[/p][p][/p][p]See you next week! :)[/p][p][/p][p][i]-Encabulated Games[/i][/p]

notes.title: 🤍 Sunday Devlog 50: I 🤍 Ease Behaviors
notes.content:
[p]Hi again, it's Sunday devlog time! The new editor feature this week, as promised, is:[/p][h2]Playback and BPM![/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/60f94001c22cfea25d9b21727913311f3a83dab6.gif"][/img]
[i]It works! Yippie!![/i][/p][p][/p][p]You can now hit a pause and play button in the editor to have a song play - the feature still needs sound effects and a few visuals [i](which might take time, given there are some issues detecting errors during playback that need care to solve)[/i] but the feature fully works and you can throw any BPM into it, and no matter what BPM it works flawlessly.[/p][p][/p][p]This is thanks to a special little behavior in Flowlab called "Ease", which we'll be talking about today.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/a2f53527edef066b43ccab716e0da44510985e89.png"][/img][/p][h2]Easing![/h2][p]Ease is one of, in my opinion, Flowlab's greatest strengths as an engine. All you do is open it up, plug the values you want to start and end at in, then tell a time and dictate the type of curve you want as well as if it affects the start or end. After these couples of steps, all you have to do is send a signal once and presto, it moves between those numbers![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/cc6d4257bed4667f35799a4b42fecab39ca9803c.gif"][/img][/p][p]This concept is known as "interpolation" in programming, and Ease does a great job of wrapping it in one nice little package. You can interpolate linearly, or use quadratic, bicubic, cubic, elastic, exponential, bounce, back, quartic and a couple others. They all have different ways they transition the output from the starting number to the end one, and it takes some experimentation to find which one is right for any situation.[/p][p][/p][p]But the thing about eases is that, because they're so intuitive, they're used a [b][i]lot[/i][/b]. Eases are used to:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/2beb14331c8ef88db2b66d01a4909b824e315973.png"][/img][/p][p]Move the camera around in the level select,[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/73c1cf972a27b431c4ae0a89fc96ecae68954f6e.png"][/img][/p][p]Make multiple objects bounce when a BPM timer tells them to,[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/a12df4a2a3bf396f74859cabcabda1cbc05260c8.png"][/img][/p][p]Animate all of the UI buttons in the game,[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/86f1f34482669d947e9a4bcf9ae09be397d04b73.png"][/img][/p][p]Handle transition effects,[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/0426b6dbbf971e7dd6c7e0f4674183264f1805b9.png"][/img][/p][p]And even control the slash effects that happen when you hit errors.[/p][p][/p][p]A lot of people like to call Encabulated Games creations "well animated" and "visually appealing", and the neat thing is that eases are actually the thing that powers a lot of that. Eases make it incredibly easy to just add animation to anything; a UI window, a particle effect, a button.. practically anything that should move, really. God bless the ease behavior!![/p][p][/p][h2]Next Week..[/h2][p]I'm moving back to college [i](and getting oriented)[/i] for the second half of next week, so I'm unaware how much work can get done before and after that period. The next goal is to add audio to the playback system and sound effects/visual effects when errors are hit, so we'll have to see how much of that gets done. Thanks for following the devlogs, and see you again in a week :).[/p][p][/p][p][i]-Encabulated Games[/i][/p]

notes.title: 🔢 Sunday Devlog 49: Encoding
notes.content: [p]We're back! Over the jam, Encabulated Games produced [url="https://flowlab.io/game/play/2822908"]Tidal Reign[/url], and it was a crazy ton of fun to work on, but that's besides the point - it's time to talk about the progress on the editor![/p][p][/p][h2]Error Placement![/h2][p]The newest [i](and coolest)[/i] thing about the editor is that you can now place errors in it properly! Take a look:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/87efedb9fe863d7a79953687819361bbf10f831c.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]Isn't it beautiful!?[/i][/p][p][/p][p]This system was actually programmed by Rezarg, the one responsible for the achievement, discord rich presence and other features. I, in turn, did my best to give the placement system some visual flare (still working on it). [/p][p][/p][p]How the note placement currently works is that you can place errors anywhere on a line with left click - and then delete them by clicking on the error with left click again. To be honest, this felt a little counter-intuitive when I first used it, and I'm rather used to deleting with right click.[/p][p][/p][p]Obviously there is a balance between making the UI juicy and not overdoing it, causing the editor to be cumbersome to use due to everything moving and bouncing. I think?? I've been balancing it well. Obviously our goal is to make the editor as [i]fun[/i] to use as possible.[/p][p][/p][p]If YOU have any thoughts on this placement system, regarding how it looks or its mechanics, please don't hesitate to inform us on them! Most of the dev team hasn't really used level editors for rhythm games, so we're learning as we go.[/p][p][/p][h2]Next Up..[/h2][p]This week was a little slow due to some personal things, the end of the Flowjam [i](I run a livestream at the end of each one, as well as playing and rating them all)[/i]. Next week I am also going to be doing work on a "large" update for Tidal Reign that should take around half the week. BUT!!! Online classes are essentially done at this point, with only one rather easy hurdle left to clear [i](after all of the really annoying ones launched at me this summer)[/i]. I was sort of forced to learn how to maximize my productivity during the Flowjam and I'm really looking forward to continuing that for the rest of the summer [i](and beyond)[/i].[/p][p][/p][p]Next week, playback and BPM will get work done.. we'll see how much time and energy it'll take to build, though. Only one way to find out :) See you next week![/p][p][/p][p][i]-Encabulated Games[/i][/p]

notes.title: 🧱 Sunday Devlog 48: Building Blocks
notes.content: [p]Hi again! It's been a bit![/p][p][/p][p]A summer trip combined with difficult online classes has made the past couple weeks hard to handle - but we're back now, and with some cool new changes to the editor. Let's take a look! :)[/p][p][/p][h2]Editor Progress[/h2][p]Here's a screenshot of the interface now:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/d1e7ad6c0f0c80f707269afc6144baea3c9f8870.png"][/img][/p][p]There are a couple new things here - first, the "temperature changes" that take place in a level are now visible! But the two more interesting things are the selection menu and scrollbar, so let's talk about them.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/a510dc9f7f4ffdb32c77d8205e9d85df87786c67.gif"][/img][/p][p]A lot of the icons on the selection menu has to be redone over and over again. Since errors in Parse are squares layered over each other, I figured that doing something similar with the icons would be cool. But it turns out, when you have solid shapes and lines instead of randomized squishing and stretching like the errors, it's a lot harder to make it look decent. So in the end I had to go with the most boring but ultimately most readable option: a boring square with a plus or minus. Making the other icons was relatively straightforward, however.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/ce79d1879f4d8f6fa52514251bc3e5cf9dd8d8a3.gif"][/img][/p][p]As for the scrollbar, this was actually made by one of our new additions to the dev team, Rezarg! He did a really great job with this scroll system, and all I had to do was animate and sprite it properly. I also added two buttons that instantly send you to the start and the end of the level for convenience :).[/p][p][/p][h2]The Summer Flowjam 2025[/h2][p]So, the engine we use, Flowlab, is having it's bi-annual flowjam event again, and this time despite everything I'm trying to really hone in on it, since it's been a while since a genuine full effort game. Thus, parse development will be out for the next two weeks, though we'll get back to it right after! Thus, you can expect the next Sunday log on Aug 10 (and that's a promise, there isn't anything major in the way that week).[/p][p]As for 1.3... it's a long story, the update will probably not be merged with 2.0 but it's starting to become a possibility as bugfixing just gets delayed and delayed. Both me and the engine developer seem to never stop being busy, and it's really hard to tell when the critical 1.3 crashing bugs will be fixed. I'm hoping we can get a foothold amidst the jam [i](as a kind of 'side quest')[/i], but we'll have to see.[/p][p][/p][p]Thanks for reading the devlog as always, and for my Flowlab friends, happy flowjamming! :)[/p][p][i]-Encabulated Games[/i][/p]

notes.title: 🌐 Monday Devlog 47: Rendering
notes.content: [p]Welcome back![/p][p][/p][p]This week.. well, summer online classes AND a very, very long two week road trip started for me. So, it's been difficult to find free time that also has stable internet!! These things compound each other, since classes are online, but enough of that, let's go over some of the new level editor changes.[/p][p][/p][p]And just to clarify! We're still waiting on the engine's dev to tackle the crashing and lag-spiking issues that Parse is facing. At this rate 1.3 is going to be merged with 2.0! [i](please god no)[/i][/p][p][/p][h2]Smooth Movement![/h2][p]Using the tech that enabled smoother parser movement back in devlog 31, level editor scrolling was modified to be smoother rather than rigidly teleporting, which it used to do - you notice this same phenomenon when you scroll pretty much any site on your phone or computer - there are subtle things that smooth the vertical scrolling out, to prevent you from feeling like you're "teleporting" up and down.[/p][p][/p][p]The main new thing, though, is:[/p][p][/p][h2]Level Rendering![/h2][p]Level beatmaps can now be fully rendered and viewed in the level editor! Any beatmaps for the game can practically instantly be examined now in this very editor instead of relying on an Excel document.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/5629051cb6692f4ad43acda1157b96cb80af63d8.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]Halcyon, seen without needing to survive the error barrage![/i][/p][p][/p][p]There are still some hiccups with the system - like how the way the errors are "sticked" onto the bars means they're delayed a bit, and the dubious, evil notes briefly appearing in the top left, but these are things that are very easy to iron out. I would just prefer to focus on being able to place notes next. It's immense that I was able to get this working on the first try, without failsafes or modifications - something that almost never happens.[/p][p][/p][p]As for how it works, it's surprisingly similar to how notes are spawned in-game - each "line", when its number on the list is updated, will read that section of the sheet. Then it'll figure out where to place the note with a bit of math, and then simply spawn it there, attaching it to the bar as it moves. The original, un-optimized note spawning system ingame worked this way, although because we need to scroll backwards and forwards at any speed, the same "most efficient" solution ingame can't work here. Still, the performance metrics are showing good numbers as I test.[/p][p][/p][p]There is one thing I'm unsure about though - I noticed that the negative errors were a little hard to spot compared to the positive ones, relatively. So, I tried adding faded outlines of the opposite color for both note types:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/7a86f03dd66c86c4e145262f2124a3e04ad6cb4f.png"][/img][/p][p]Compare this to the original, without the outlines:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/baa381561efe3972a167c1f7ef1aeaf378a0fd35.png"][/img][/p][p]Does it look better? I'm not entirely sure - it seems to improve visibility, but it also is just a bit confusing to the brain. At least for me - write in the comments or Discord if you have any thoughts![/p][p][/p][h2]Up Next..[/h2][p]As I'm on a trip, and taking summer classes at the same time, it's uncertain what'll be ready by next week's devlog. However, I WOULD like to note that due to trailer shenanigans, 1.3 will not be out anytime before July 13 at the minimum. Around then I'll finally be back home and will be able to make the 1.3 trailer, and hopefully Parse will finally be freed of its bugs and crashes on export![/p][p][/p][p]Working on this level editor, however, has been extremely fun, and I regret not doing it sooner. It was lower on my priority list to other things, and I wasn't too interested in working on Parse at all around a month ago. However, working on the editor and seeing everything come together so neatly is immensely rewarding, honestly way more than something like controller navigation. So, expect the devlogs to be weekly again![/p][p][/p][p]As always, be back in a week![/p][p][/p][p][i]-Encabulated Games[/i][/p]

notes.title: Monday Devlog 46: Deigsn
notes.content:
[p]Good evening![/p][p][/p][p]This week, the war on the bugs actually got worse instead of better. Following the release of the second 1.3 open beta, more bug reports rolled in, and rampant testing ensued. Bleh.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/f5a9cba87b72213b9bd49f050f5390131249c229.png"][/img][i]Ahh, the classic Unity NullReferencException. Flowlab Edition™.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]However, there have already been a couple devlogs about debugging [i](our game attracts bugs like a rotting pot of soup in the Amazon Rainforest)[/i] So I'd like to do a deep dive into some cool new tech:[/p][p][/p][h2]Level Editor Progress![/h2][p]So, figuring out how the level editor is going to be laid out has been the topic of discussion for quite a while. Where are things going to be oriented? Will the editor be vertical or horizontal? How much versatility should there be?[/p][p][/p][p]After a lengthy discussion in the developer channel, I decided to test a vertical track for level editing. This offers less space than making the track horizontal would, but it would also be more game accurate, and it turns out that other vertical rhythm games have these kinds of editors too.[/p][p][/p][p]So, after a lot of finagling, here's the first system done: [b]scrolling![/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/adfa3be68bf7a40b3e16a3e776c840917bb9b03f.gif"][/img]
[i]You can scroll by clicking and dragging or by scrolling the mouse wheel![/i][/p][p][/p][p]Despite it seeming rather simple, getting this system to work was a bit of a headache:[/p][p][/p][p]First, Parse levels can be from 400-800 lines long on average. And having 800 objects moving around in a level editor would slow the game down so much that it wouldn't be playable. So instead, the bar objects teleport themselves to the top or bottom of the screen once they cease from view, kind of like a conveyor belt. Thanks to this, only a handful of objects need to be in the scene at all for scrolling to work :).[/p][p][/p][p]Detecting mouse movement and mouse wheels is also difficult. It took a couple of re-dos of the code to make something that worked for left-click scrolling and mouse wheel scrolling at the same time to work, but thankfully that problem sorted itself out, too.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/ebd5b852e71cd14dcbc783a22f0762a58fecd4cd.png"][/img][i]The finished system is far more elegant than the old one, thankfully.[/i][/p][p][/p][h2]Next Up:[/h2][p]Now that this UI system is done, the next steps are getting the bar pieces to change their values properly as the player scrolls, so that'll be the next step. However, that is going to take a day at most, so there should be much more to report on next devlog. It's been almost adrenaline inducing to finally be putting together this feature I've wanted for the game for so long![/p][p][/p][p]Let us know if you have any, at all, UX things to say about the editor - editor features you like, quirks you appreciate or annoy you, details in editors, etc. We want this editor to be as intuitive as the rest of the game is, so let us know your thoughts![/p][p][/p][p]Thanks for following the devlog!![/p][p][/p][p][i]-Encabulated Games[/i][/p]

notes.title: 🧪 Sunday Devlog 45: More Testing! More Testing!
notes.content:
[p]Hello! It's been a bit![/p][p]Let's cut right to the point with the most important news:[/p][p][/p][h2]1.3 Open Beta 2 & Discord Rich Presence[/h2][p]A new version of the 1.3 open beta is out! This version contains:[/p][list][*][p]Rich Presence: Parse-O-Rhythm now has full Discord Rich Presence support! The panel actually shows things when you're playing now.[/p][/*][*][p]UI Juice: Some small updates to the guide and progress bar UI to make them more informative & feel better.[/p][/*][*][p]Launcher: New changes to how the launcher & achievement system works, which should make Windows Defender less angry & the achievement system efficienter.[/p][/*][*][p]Bugfix: Music not resuming after unpausing.[/p][/*][*][p]Bugfix: Crashes relating to opening random levels.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/67e0ef107a0dd916869484f1c213202e39f4ab54.png"][/img][/p][p][i]It's so beautiful![/i][/p][p][/p][p]There are still some bugs that are afoot, and it's unclear if they've all been solved yet, which is why 1.3 is still not out yet [i](getting there lol)[/i]. Thank you so much for the bug reporting y'all have been doing! Keep it up! :)[/p][p][/p][p]So, why has it taken so long for this devlog to come out? Well..[/p][p][/p][h2]Cyberattack![/h2][p]Last weekend on a fateful May 31, an attacker got the Flowlab servers shut down. Since Flowlab is web-based, that meant we were locked out of being able to work on the engine. In addition, most art work for rich presence had been done, so without the ability to get the last bits of work done to count for a devlog, we had to sit out last weekend.[/p][p][/p][p]Thankfully, the attacker was more of a phony than any sort of serious threat, and instead of paying a fee to get the site back, Flowlab's engine dev got to work building a new server to go around the attacker. Disruptions still occurred throughout the week, but it's safe to say at this point that Flowlab is fully back up and running thanks to Grazer, Flowlab's developer's efforts. Thank you so much!!![/p][p][/p][h2]Next?[/h2][p]How soon 1.3 comes really depends on how many more bugs we encounter. The update is pretty much ready, and is available to play on the opentesting branch, but we aren't going to deliver something bug-ridden for hopefully obvious reasons.[/p][p][/p][p]In addition, the person behind the achievement, rich presence & more SDKs, Rezarg has officially joined the Encabulated Games team for Parse, which brings our total dev count to 5! Yippie!!

That'll be all for now. Thanks for bearing with everything going on! See you next week or earlier!

[i]-Encabulated Games[/i][/p]

notes.title: 🎵 Monday Devlog 44: Music Notes
notes.content:
Welcome back!

So.. about there not being a devlog last week. Long story short, life has been getting in the way lately. It’s nothing dire, and progress on the game is moving, BUT a lot of things that I was supposed to get done during my semester got pushed into now by the semester itself, since it was so busy. The result is that the start of summer has been messy!! However, things have been stabilizing again, and productivity will ramp back up this week!

[h2]Where Are We?[/h2]
At the moment, I’m currently working on adding [b]discord rich presence[/b] to the game and [b]updating the achievement system[/b] so Windows Defender doesn’t get mad at it anymore [i](+ other nice benefits)[/i]. This is all thanks to the advanced technologies Rezarg has been cooking up [i](he should honestly just be added to the dev team at this point lol)[/i].

However, for this devlog, I’ll be handing off the mic to the three music artists who work on the game, so they can discuss their plans for the music in 2.0! None of them have actually written in the devlogs before and It’s starting to feel too weird that I keep writing “we” when I’m the only person who ever writes these, lol. I’ll be passing the mic over to boxlion now so she can discuss her plans :).

[h2]Boxlion's Portion[/h2]
Heyo! :3 I’m thatboxlion, and I’m the composer for the Sweets album! I'm honored to compose another album for 2.0, and I've got a couple of ideas that I’m excited to start brainstorming with >:]. I’m planning on making 4 to 5 songs, and I’m hoping to make them even better than the Sweets album was! 

If you wanna see some of my own stuff (I’m also a game dev :]), I’ve got a [url=https://discord.gg/NexwZCK3Yn]discord server[/url] too! You can also listen to the [url=https://open.spotify.com/album/129kV8hNnCuhL3lTmj97YM?si=LzOeXId_Taa52XkCvHx6cQ]Sweets album[/url] on spotify, if you didn’t know ‘,:]. That’s my bit, now I’ll pass the mic off to Logan for his plans! 

[h2]Logan's Portion[/h2]
Hi all!

This is Logan. It’s weird that this is my first time writing to you all in a devlog. As of a few days ago, the semester has come to an end, and I’m ready to come back to this game. I’m excited to share a few plans I have for the 2.0 update. These concepts are still a little early and they are subject to change. That means that feedback from you would be very helpful!

Firstly, I would like to share a bit of a personal project that I’ve been working on for a while. I’m working on an album! I had to put a pause on it due to school, but now that the semester’s over, I’m excited to get to work on it again. I don’t have any more to share about it at this time, but select tracks from it will be included in the 2.0 update. 

Another thing that could be coming to the update is a collection of remixes of tracks from Galacdrive. I’ll be honest, I’ve learned a ton since the Galacdrive era, and it would be fun to flex a bit of that gained experience to create new amped up versions of those tracks. [b]You can let me know your thoughts as well as some of your favorite tracks that you think I should remix.[/b]

With school wrapping up, I’m turning more to this project to put my energy into. I’m looking forward to engaging more with this amazing community. I’m taking inspiration from Jackson, who does so much for this community. I have no idea how he gets one of these out every week. 
Thanks for sticking with us!

[h2]Prism4ticturtle's Portion[/h2]
Hello, Prism here! I’m the composer of the Dreams album and I’m thrilled to be back for another album for 2.0! This time I’m considering a more intense/frantic album, maybe even utilizing some of the distorted vocals I’ve been playing around with recently. While I am still in the theorycrafting stage as of now, I look forward to sharing my progress with you all soon! 

If you like what you hear, I’ve got a [url=https://open.spotify.com/artist/6XfLiWzP6gTojlNb2BfF2I?si=HGX-y070SbevXCtjtAprTQ]Spotify[/url] now where you can listen to Dreams along with some of my other works!

That’s all from me, see ya! :)

[h2]Wrapping up..[/h2]
While I [i]predict[/i] 1.3 will release sometime this week, I don't want to guarantee anything - things seem to derail so often and so quickly that I think it's just best that new features are announced when they should be, lol. In addition, some drafting for the layout of the level editor has been made, and we're messing around with it behind closed doors. More info will be revealed later :).

notes.title: 🔄 Sunday Devlog 41: Re-Working
notes.content:
Welcome back yet again! This devlog is going to cover the past two weeks, since the announcement about the 1.3 public beta was last week [i](roughly)[/i].

In order to get 1.3 out the door, a lot of stuff, unexpectedly, had to be completely re-done before the update could be released, causing it to be delayed by a couple days. Let's talk about these features in this devlog!

[h2]Controller Navigation System[/h2]
It all started a couple days before the release, when pausing was going through a final round of testing. You see, the way controller navigation works in the game is with an invisible "cursor controller" object that seeks out button "hitboxes" [i](which are also invisible)[/i]. When I have them enabled, the hitboxes look like this: 
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/34de774ce3709555cef9dc5273b05b2cfc237b85.gif[/img]

When the player hits the D-pad, the following things happen in order: [list]
[*]The cursor controller fires a ray [i](imagine a laser pointer)[/i] in the D-pad direction.
[*]If the ray hits any cursor hitbox object, it sends the coordinates of the object back to the controller cursor.
[*]The cursor controller spawns a tiny object at the found coordinates.
[*]The tiny object, upon collision with the cursor hitbox due to being the same coordinates, deletes itself.
[*]At the same time, the cursor hitbox notices it's collided with the tiny object, and notifies the button it's paired to that it's selected. [/list]Despite all this, there was a pretty significant problem. When the game is paused, this also means physics are paused, and thus, [b]collisions cannot occur[/b], which breaks the controller navigation system during a game pause. So, I needed to implement a new method that didn't use the coordinate and collision system at all.

However, what I discovered during this refactoring is that the controller navigation was possibly one of the worst things I've ever programmed. Functions had no use, signals went nowhere, there were chunks of circuitry with seemingly no purpose. So for the next two fateful days, instead of launching the 1.3 public beta, [i]I ripped out tons of the controller navigation code[/i] for a way cleaner solution. The logic is still quite a lot for a devlog, but rest assured, the new method is actually comprehensible, expandable, and predictable. Phew.

[h2]Achievement System[/h2]
During all of this, Rezarg, the one behind the game's achievement system, has been continuously revising the achievement bundle. The achievement system works by sending a request to a server, which then relays it to Steam - but this costs money to run, and the current way Parse's achievements was working was sending far more requests than were needed, clogging things up and causing bloat.

So, despite the end result looking way more tangled, the new achievement bundle is far simpler to use, is more efficient on requests, and doesn't get stuck in loops like the old system did!!

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/995c8815b12c10ba32c4c0f9c3b66b381c971db8.png[/img]

Recently, recently Rezarg came up with an [b][i]even better [/i][/b]solution that doesn't even require sending any pings to an external server, can register achievements far more quickly, is more secure and won't provoke Windows Defender as much! On top of being free to run compared to the old solution, this version can also work with other Steam features as well, such as DLCs and the [b]Steam Workshop[/b]!! The new achievement infrastructure will be implemented before 1.3 fully releases in a week.

[h2]What's coming up?[/h2]
My semester is beginning to wrap up at this time, so the only thing that'll be done this upcoming week is bug fixes for 1.3 and releasing it hopefully by the next weekend. I'm super excited to finally release this update with all its juicy features and get to work on 2.0! Thanks for following the devlog as always :)

[i]-Encabulated Games[/i]

notes.title: 🔃 Sunday Devlog 38: Doodad Emporium
notes.content:
Hey, sorry to keep you waiting an extra week! Truthfully, taking 19 college credits and three major projects [i](including this one)[/i] was a [b]grave[/b] mistake, but I think that's obvious enough from the previous logs.

At the moment, the heavily lifted features for 1.3 are waiting on controller support on the engine side [i](this has been going on for a while...)[/i] as well as some engine-side bug fixes as well. I've been doing my best to help get those resolved by working with the engine dev, but oh boy is development messy.

So, for this log, allow me to showcase some funny circuits 1.3 utilizes and how they'll be running the upcoming major update!

[h2]1.3's Circuits[/h2]
Starting off, we have the:

[h3][b]Achievement Registrar[/b][/h3]

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/7d9680919fc789261b2472506e863a32a08a9f0e.png[/img]
This group's job is to send a signal into the "SAI" bundle at the end, the achievement bundle that was successfully tested last devlog.

So, why's there all this random stuff around it? Well, the thing is, the achievement system can only successfully register one achievement per three seconds. Because of this, if multiple achievements get activated at the same time, there needs to be a way to ensure that the "pending" achievements have their shot. So, the timer placed before the text that activates the achievement is there to send a new signal every three seconds, until the achievement bundle sends a signal out confirming the achievement.

After it does this, it disables the timer so it stops sending requests over and over. In addition, it sends a signal to a saved value that ensures that a signal is never mistakenly sent to activate the achievement again, further helping minimize clogging.

There are very few situations with the achievements where you can get multiple in a row, but it's a very real possibility. This system allows the achievement system to work in a much safer way!


[h3][b]Controller Nav Configurator[/b][/h3]

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/0ba981be9ab4f918ebb11248728e9e4c98a167d2.png[/img]

The actual controller navigation system is complicated, a little messy and very spread out. Most circuits would take a while, so here's a simpler one. This group of values that go to message behaviors get whatever info is necessary for the controller nav target to work.

The controller navigation system works by having an invisible object shoot a ray out in the direction of the D-pad to find a button to select, and it then teleports itself to that button. This sounds like an odd method, but this way allows button layouts to be visually edited.

This visual editing is enhanced by this group of behaviors here - you can set how big you want the target to be in terms of X [i](width)[/i] and Y [i](height)[/i], you can set if the raycaster should start at this specific button on the level start, what scenarios permit the button to be selectable at all, and more. This took a lot of extra work to set up, but it means that adding new menus is a complete breeze!


[h3][b]Level List Assigner[/b][/h3]

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/8cbc476ca6899180647646919778e651df4b96ea.png[/img]
In Sunday Devlog 32 and 33, a level list feature was shown that displays all of the levels in the game in a big list.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/839bc32b557443e04283af3d27fe355e8e739455.gif[/img]

The way each object knows what level info to display is determined by the code above. When you flip through the list, you're not actually flipping through separate objects - instead, the objects themselves change themselves to display the info for a different level!

Put simply, when you press the left or right arrow, it updates this value inside all of the level lists that tells them what page they're on. The filters above and below the number behavior allow the pages to loop if you go beyond page 5 or further back than page 1. 

From there, an expression takes the list, along with a value that determines what place in the list it is [i](the name)[/i], and uses this to figure out which number, representing a level, the list object should display.

You may also notice a section at the end labelled "17 erasure". Essentially, the warp album was originally planned to have four levels instead of three, so the numbers for all of the levels got assigned back then. By the time we learnt that the album would actually have three, it would have taken more time to update the numbers for all of the other levels across different parts in the game. So instead, every time the levels are listed, the code just makes sure to pretend 17 doesn't exist and outputs the next highest number instead :P.

[h2]Wrapping Up[/h2]
Truthfully, I'm not aware at what point the engine shenanigans will be fixed up enough for public testing to start. On top of that, I'm once again getting weighed down by schoolwork a lot, which is why this devlog is coming a little late [i](sorry ;-;)[/i].

For now I'm unaware of how much is coming for the future, but regardless, 1.3 being so close in general is really exciting! I can't wait for everyone to eventually get to enjoy everything we've been cooking up the past couple months. Thanks for reading as always.

notes.title: 💡 Sunday Devlog 37: Eureka!
notes.content:
Welcome back! This week was a bit of tying up loose ends, but there's also some neat new community-made tech to talk about as well. Let's dive right in!

[h2]Functional Achievements![/h2]
Roughly a week and a half ago, one of Flowlab's community members who goes by "Rezarg" came out with a tool that he's been cooking up for the past couple of weeks. Basically, any Flowlab game can be activated through this launcher, and with the right configs, it will allow a game to just trigger achievement unlocks. 

The really incredible thing about this tool is that it's not built into the engine, and rather uses external tools to relay a message to Steam to unlock achievements for the player. It is one of the first times that third party tools are being integrated into a game outside of the engine supporting it!

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/43ef28ba11da9dc00fbf870d7802702134e689b3.png[/img]
[i]It's not really expressed in this screenshot well, but Rezarg got some much-deserved love from the community for pulling this off.[/i]

So, naturally, I was extremely eager to test this out. The weird thing with Steam achievements is that unlike other features, you can't have them locked in a beta branch - once you add them, they're rolled out to [b][i]everyone, immediately[/i][/b].

Therefore, our older game, [i]Envoy[/i], was used as the lab rat for this achievement test. A couple funky bugs were found and fixed along the way, but lo and behold, I managed to get a working achievement in for Envoy through Rezarg's tool. Huzzah!

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/42fdfca68d33774f2278da6f5488ad8d18cad995.png[/img]
[i]I was practically jumping out of my seat at the sight of this. As a slight disclaimer, a couple engine updates have made Envoy much more challenging to fully support, so this achievement was only activated on a test branch. It was recalled right after this experiment concluded, lol.[/i]

With that, all of the achievements were thrown into Parse-O-Rhythm, and while they aren't available yet [i](since 1.3 needs to be released first)[/i], they're all typed and uploaded into Steamworks, which took a good hour and a half of naming, exporting, naming, assigning, over and over.. for all [b]31 [/b]achievements!

[h2]Bugfixing[/h2]
The other thing that went on this week was bugfixing for the game. While the wonky easing bug [i](from last devlog[/i]) wasn't patched this week, many more bugs relating to slashing, RGB issues on the combo counter, and certain settings not getting applied have been patched, so pausing will be more-or-less done once the easing bug is fixed by the engine developer.

[h2]What's Left?[/h2]
At this point, there are only a couple things left for [b]1.3[/b]: the achievements, pausing, and controller update. These are mainly:

-Making the controller interface with the new menus [i](easy)[/i]
-Ironing out everything after the easing bug is fixed [i](medium)[/i]
-Adding the code to support the Steam achievements on the game's end [i](medium)[/i]

Truth be told, I've still got a lot on my plate as I return to school. With that said, pretty much all of the super-heavy, time consuming things have been ironed out by this point, so it's safe to say that you can expect an open beta within the next week or two :).

[i][b]Also![/b][/i] The game will be going on sale again for the Steam Spring Sale, this time for [b]30% off![/b] This would be a great time to get the game for a friend, invest in it yourself, or maybe even tell others about it :). The sale will last a week and it starts on March 13th, so I hope to see you then.

Thanks for following the dev logs as always!

notes.title: 🐞Sunday Devlog 36: BUGS BUGS BUGS BUGS BUGS BUGS
notes.content:
Time to buy some raid bug repellant.

[h2]BUGS.[/h2]
Ok, well technically, this week I finally finished the countdown system, which means that pausing is now a fully functional feature. It even [b]accounts for the BPM[/b] of whatever song you're playing, which makes resuming feel more natural :).

Fully functional is really overselling it though - not that it doesn't work, but because of the sheer amount of bugs that clog it up as if insects overran the internals of a car engine. 

So, here's what it looks like:

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/efa7d8ba53ec887c6d4b9eaa99c76bcf3a4e9e21.gif[/img]

This clearly is a little out of whack, but the main thing to focus on is the countdown UI - why does it go all haywire when the game resumes?

Well, some couple weeks ago, people on the Flowlab discord (the server for the engine this game uses) started reporting on how pausing would mess with the "ease" behavior. Encabulated games run on easing as it makes it incredibly easy to make something bounce, pop, or just move smoothly with a single behavior.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/8b5cff3a1adbed50ccf40182789cda2d5a749de0.png[/img]
[i]Inside the cursor code, two eases are used to make the cursor change size when you left and right click, as well as letting go of the respective mouse buttons.[/i]

However, when a game is paused in Flowlab, any eases that run seem to forget that they're still unpaused.. partly. Which means that the more an ease runs while a game is paused, the more dramatically different the output will be once it's [b][i]un[/i][/b]paused.

..And this is how absolutely bonkers numbers like these end up showing when debugging the code:

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/c890abdb24290ca0165c96c3ce03bc08e4407201.png[/img]
Why exactly does this happen? I didn't program the engine, so it's beyond me. But since this engine bug is quick and easy to replicate, it should be sorted within this week. Oh.. and as for the bugs I'm responsible for myself, those will also be getting patched up this week.
[h2]
Wrapping up..[/h2]
Thanks to my break finally starting, I'll be able to report on much more next Sunday. In fact, I'd be willing to wager that 1.3 will be fully ready for launch by next week.. although testing will have to commence regardless. Thanks for reading :).

[i]-Encabulated Games[/i]

notes.title: 🧊 Sunday Devlog 34: Get Icced, Dummy.
notes.content:
Instantaneously, a frigid freeze flashes in the air, and before you know it, you've been encased in a cube of ice: unable to move for all of eternity. Get Icced, Dummy. 

..At least, that's what would happen if the game had to follow medieval magic logic. Fortunately, we can achieve the same effect minus the ice with code!

[h2]Pausing![/h2]
This week has seen the beginnings of the new pausing feature, so let's go over its plans and then cover current progress.

Mechanically, [b]pausing a file is going to replace leaving the file[/b]. This means that whatever key you had binded to "ExitFile" is now going to [i]pause[/i] the game instead. From the pause screen, you can simply go back to the level select [i](or restart)[/i] from there. After some feedback from a friend, Esc is also hard-coded to pause the game during play as well, just as a failsafe.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/3437e2f65602596218cb1a1e62e81bd30ec79fea.png[/img]

The pause screen is going to be the exact same layout as the options menu in the homescreen, with all the same settings. A lot of why pausing isn't done yet is due to the fact that all of these settings need to work as soon as you resume the game or exit it. You'll even be able to change your character!

Anyway, while you can [i]technically[/i] pause the game at the moment, the rest of the game wasn't built for it, so it kind of combusts when you do it. I'm going to have to work through a lot of bugs and weird scenarios [i](and probably insider testing)[/i] before this can get checked for shipping, lol.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/9501a4757c142bd2715157f1d4525bf9f88fecef.gif[/img]
[i]There are a couple.. uhh.. "quirks" here that'll have to be ironed out.[/i]

Some more things are planned for pausing, such as a countdown when you unpause before the game starts again, and other quality-of-life things. However, I think it's a better idea to show these mechanics rather than continue typing about them.

[h2]Up Next[/h2]
I've been getting more efficient with my work outside of this project, however, a game jam at my school is coming up this coming weekend. I can guarantee a devlog, but I can't guarantee the pausing feature being [i]completely[/i] done. I'll try, though! :P

After pausing, all of the major features for 1.3 will be ready - except achievements. At the moment, we're still waiting on the engine's support for Steam achievements to be realized. If we complete 1.3 before that happens, we'll probably just start on 2.0 work in the background until achievements are ready. There'll be stuff we can post about, and other stuff that's better to be revealed later :).

Thanks as always for reading these devlogs! They're honestly the main reason I still make progress on this game, even when the pressure from everything else is as immense as ever. But fortunately, that pressure is only going to be so high for two more weeks.

notes.title: 🧽 Sunday Devlog 31: Smoothing It Out
notes.content:
Hey! Welcome back to the Sunday Devlogs: 2025 edition! Here we go!

You can read up on what we've been up to the past couple weeks on the Discord (spoiler alert: not this game!) but now that we're back, I figured I'd start the new year by tackling a really big personal pet peeve of mine.

[h2]Parser Jitter[/h2]
When you strafe your parser back and forth, you may notice that it tends to get pretty jittery - the rotation and movement can "budge" around, which looks wonky, to say the least.

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/3a3daeca3115fa7ee57f60501292652adae9c4e5.gif[/img]
[i]GIF slowed down 50% to see the jitter a bit better[/i]

This has always been really annoying to me, since I really care about our projects being as smooth as can be. It happens on fast computers, slow computers, the web and Steam versions. It's always been there. For the longest time, I tried to figure out ways to fix it to no avail. Convoluted "velocity-based" systems were overly complex and impossible to calibrate right, ease-based systems froze the parser in place.

However, since the game jam we partook in, a certain "interpolation" bundle offered another way to smoothly animate something without the bureaucracy of eases. Maybe this was the key..

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/44bdaf49d236df7217241fa8de006a5cf6b501a8.png[/img]

..And indeed, it was! After a little bit of fine tuning, strafing the parser is now way, way smoother. [i]Shockingly[/i] smooth to be honest. I wonder if the authors of that bundle laced it with anything.

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/814374b53cd9c39e8a837d119cb41bb1d292f6dd.gif[/img]
[i]This GIF also slowed down to 50%.[/i]

This does come with a tradeoff, though - because of the way it "smooths" the player's mouse movements, the parser can lag behind the mouse. However, this is impossible to notice when playing any levels in the game, and will really only affect you if you play custom levels beyond what the game can throw at you. Regardless, it's been made a setting™ just in case you'd like to disable it.

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/1fc3a3c103c888eea7581624e67330686c134e2f.png[/img]

[h2]Controller Support Part 6: Electric Bickalix[/h2]
At this point, it's been so long since 1.2 Part 1 came out, and it's so close to the release of [b]Steam achievements[/b] for the engine, that controller support is going to be moved to the 1.3 update instead. By the time this update releases, the puzzle of controllers will [i](hopefully)[/i] be finally solved, done and dusted.

I'm aware that like, probably 2 people are concerned at all about controller support. However, when custom levels inevitably arrive, that number will almost certainly be greater. And that aside, why not have some extra things to show off on the Steam page with high quality implementation to boot?

Sorry this devlog was a little short again - I've been getting back into the college routine as things settle back into place, and good lord, there are things to do!! It's a lot, but it's rewarding to finish the day after grinding out lots of work across a myriad of classes, career building, and yes, this game.

Thanks for following the devlogs as always, and see you again in a week :).

notes.title: Sunday Devlog 30: Year One
notes.content:
[b]Hi again![/b]

Roughly around this time, one year ago, Parse-O-Rhythm began development for the Winter Flowjam 2024. It was made in the span of two weeks for the jam, and despite [b]blatantly ignoring the jam theme[/b], the game was beloved by the community, rocketed to first place, and became the most played game on Flowlab.io [i](the site it is made on)[/i] for 2024, as well as the most played and liked Encabulated Games title ever in the [b]~4 years[/b] of our existence.

Despite sub-par sales, egregious engine limitations, murky marketing and relentlessly slow game updates, I've come to remind myself this Christmas that even though we didn't make as much of a splash as we wanted to on Steam [i](so far)[/i], we still ended up putting together one hell of a game. One year ago we were just mobile game makers, and the year before that we were naught but feeble webgame developers. We've come a long way and have learned a lot, and we aren't done with Parse-O-Rhythm yet or for a long time, which is something to celebrate!

[h2]Let's Try Something Different[/h2]
All of that mushy stuff aside, let's recap the first two weeks of development of the game. Before the devlogs began, and before "Parse-O-Rhythm" was even decided as a name. [b][i]Let's go all the way back, one year ago...[/i][/b]

[h2]The initial concept[/h2]
Before the two week game jam even started, we wanted to make some kind of rhythm game where you hit things that come from the top of the screen using the mouse. A week prior, I put together a quick prototype to make sure that the idea was enjoyable. By the time the jam kicked off. We had a really basic character movement and falling note framework to work with.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/ceb016b6332fe4acc0d4561084e5723e06d504f9.png[/img]
[i]The first picture of the game, taken from the dev channel[/i]

One of the first things we needed to quickly figure out was what our game was going to look like and be themed around. I asked Logan (Bean) if he wanted to make any kind of music in particular, and after a short conversation we decided that a game themed around programming/hacking with edm/techno music would be the way to go. Music samples were shared, and a small illustration of what the game may be was sketched up.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/5ff28070185e07c50280558d66251a979e70d5db.png[/img]
[i]Testing out the randomized characters & colored "errors"[/i]

[h2]Beginning construction[/h2]
One part of the Encabulated Games workflow that is a bit uncommon for a game jam is that art and code are worked on in parallel. There's this psychological motivation I get while building a game that only triggers when I can actually see something coming to life, so throughout the first two days, visual effects were created as the note slashing system got more fleshed out, and the sprites for the main game were drawn and decided upon.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/0875d90b33ab1a374cdfe60c0895f5583a52d9c0.png[/img]
[i]These flashy effects, and later most of the other colors in the whole game, were done using a rendering effect called "color dodge". It basically gives colors luminosity, which is great for lighting effects for any game or art project.[/i]

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/ff103fe9f007b3de58e5556a9fd008ffa0aa20e3.png[/img]
[i]The style of the player was formed very quickly and wasn't changed much throughout development.[/i]

[h2]Problems Start Arising[/h2]
Now, the engine we use, Flowlab, is a remarkable engine for making something quickly. However, it's only used to a couple dozen to a couple hundred objects to keep track of and simulate. While the engine got a big performance update this year, at the time, the engine was more limited. We had songs set up where all the notes were pre-placed in scene, and would fall down via the physics system. It worked, but hundreds of physics objects was hard for the game to handle.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/dc438e1ee277741d686b20b3511fc98b13bb457a.png[/img]
[i]Notes used to look like this in the scene editor.[/i]

To get around this, we had to make an entire new system for the notes. This new system would read a number list and "print" them on the screen to the same BPM of the music. The technical details are a little much, but safe to say that it left my brain sufficiently cooked. Fortunately, this reduced the amount of objects in a scene from ~2400 to [b]~200[/b], significantly improving performance and allowing the game to run on nearly all machines.

In addition, the slashing system used to be more primitive, and you could actually hit multiple close notes with the same slash. Unfortunately though, the game actually finished the game jam with this issue still present, because work on the actual levels and all of the UI still urgently needed work.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/b11a9ac1f91a89058aaf8db79d31048f8e868d78.png[/img]
[i]The ancient, forbidden multi-error slash.[/i]

[h2]The Rush[/h2]
[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/cb35daf9c86c0298d072950d8960406d5d90eacf.png[/img]
[i]The Encabulated Games fashion of cooking so late that the barrier between late at night and early in the morning is shattered like a pane of glass.[/i]

The second week of the jam was much less interesting than the first.. to write about. The middle of the jam crept up to us, and with barely fleshed out UI and songs still to map, week two was a turbo-rush to finish the game, at the same time I was going back to college and Logan was going on a short trip.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/c501c3af1ba0e49bffa16d41e666e256bdb797e4.png[/img]
[i]The (frankly overcomplicated) level select kept getting re-dos and more and more polish, which took a lot of framework to get right.[/i]

As I slaved away in Google Sheets making the levels, and Logan slaved away in Logic Pro making the other 60% of the soundtrack, it often looked like we would be unable to deliver four songs and the full game on time.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/0b8cacf1244be9db43222f949f795f8d4f9d3903.png[/img]
..especially as I started to get so distracted by the game itself that I wasn't building the actual levels

However, through those hellish past few days of basically no breaks aside from when absolutely necessary [i]("eating", sleeping, and going to class)[/i], we did eventually deliver Parse-O-Rhythm, albeit with a couple bugs like the multi-error slash issue and a weird framerate dropping problem. And then, well, the rest was history.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/45b455ac6beb6ad9d9d73e0ff1f7660d72b55fd4.png[/img]

[h2]Future Of The Game[/h2]
Heading into the new year, Parse-O-Rhythm is going to remain our main game! [b]The Winter Flowjam 2025[/b] is currently in session for the next [b]two weeks[/b], so we are working on our submission to it for those next two weeks. The only thing you should expect during these next two weeks is the announcement of the [b]soundtrack release[/b], which is imminent to come this week! After these two weeks are over, work will resume on Parse-O-Rhythm again.

I would like to also note: on the discord, a poll is being hosted this week on if Sunday devlogs should continue as weekly events, or if they should be bi-weekly or monthly. We don't want to spam up the Steam page too much, so let us know what you think about all that on the discord!

With achievements, controller support [i](so sorry ;-;)[/i], and custom levels on the horizon for 2025, this next year is going to be one hell of a year for the game in brand new ways. Thank you for being part of the journey so far. We made a post on the discord already about it, but [b]making games would be pointless if no one got to enjoy them.[/b] And once custom levels are out, I'm certain that many more will be able to enjoy our Parse-O-Rhythm in brand new and awesome ways.

See you in the next devlog!

[i]-Encabulated Games[/i]

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/d5fff540b421138c3dde1b898a0ad82bc83bfd85.gif[/img]

That being said, hopefully some time from the engine's developer can be allocated to solving the problem - despite the distance between 1.2 part 1 and now, we're still working on it!

Thanks for reading as always. Catch you next week!

notes.title: 🔭 Sunday Devlog 26: Looking Ahead
notes.content:
Hey! Now that 1.2 is largely done (at least at the development level), let's talk about what's in store for 1.3 and why it's a little foggy with this one.

[h2]The fuzziness of 1.3[/h2]
1.3 will have some features that are guaranteed, and other features that are more on the whim on if they are made for the engine in time. The thing about the game engine we use, Flowlab. is that it used to just be a classroom tool to teach kids how to code. It's only in the past couple years that the engine has been used to create genuine commercial games, and since its programming language is entirely tied to the engine, the engine has had a lot of missing features that have been gradually added over the years. This is why the game lacks things like mouse locking or achievements.

Because of this, we don't exactly know everything that is to come in 1.3. However, we can still share a list of what [i][b]will [/b][/i]be in the update, and what [b][i]could [/i][/b]be:

[h2]Guaranteed Features[/h2]
- Pausing during gameplay
- A list of all tracks and your scores/ranks for each
- Improved audio, such as adaptive music for albums & pitch variation for sound effects like slashes
- Ability to invert the player to be black rather than white, which can help visibility
- Improved UI for the results screen

[h2]Potential Features[/h2]
- Custom characters [i](draw your own or just link a png to have a fully custom parser & weapon)[/i]
- Steam achievements
- Cursor locking [i](vertical and/or in-screen)[/i]

As said before, these features rest on if they gain engine support by the time the other features are done.

[h2]The Roadmap[/h2]
As visualized below, 1.3 is the only update left before 2.0 begins development. For all of the [b]potential features[/b] above, if they aren't implemented for 1.3, you can expect them to be ready for 2.0.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/ed3ceeb5050506405bc55dbdee8a566d0caac6f0.png[/img]

Regardless, Sunday Devlogs will continue to be posted as development goes on. I don't have anything brand new to report this week other than the 1.2 launch because of school projects & Thanksgiving, but I'll be back to work on Parse-O-Rhythm this week. Till then, and thanks for reading!

[i]-Encabulated Games[/i]

notes.title: 🌌 1.2.0 Part 1: The Galactic Update!
notes.content:
Yo! After over two months, the first part of the 1.2 update is launching today! Controller & Steam Deck support are also ready, but they're waiting on an engine bug that's due to be fixed in around a week from now. Let's talk about what's now available in 1.2 part 1! :)

[h2]Level Select Overhaul[/h2]
The album select for the game has been replaced with an expandable [b]galaxy map[/b], with its own adaptive music [i](courtesy of boxlion)[/i] and a nonlinear progression path. 

This way, it's a lot easier to tell where files lead to, and you don't feel pressured to try the difficult sweets album right out of the gate. Since the old album select was a badly sorted vertical list, this new one should ease you into the game in a smoother way, unless you really wanna challenge yourself and go for the hard albums first!

Albums in the game have also been given [b]subtle background improvements[/b] with floating background elements when inside them!

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/a71b287412159e4fbdfdd3590583ec208dacf610.gif[/img]
[i]Brand new map![/i]

[h2]Upgraded Keybindings & UI[/h2]
You can now [b]change the keybinds for restarting and exiting files[/b], as well as [b]binding more keys[/b]. You can now map unorthodox keys like Ctrl, Shift, Tab, or Backspace to anything you want if you wish to!

The default keybindings for restarting and exiting files have also been changed to [b]R[/b] and [b]Esc[/b] respectively.

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/b74e1bdb8a8e874378a25cbdaf5d6467a498ef8f.gif[/img]

[b]The UI for the settings menu has also been improved[/b], with some flavor elements and iconography!

[h2]Better Startup Screen[/h2]
The game has a [b]new and improved startup screen[/b] that gets you into the game in around a third of the time it used to, by skipping past unnecessary cutscenes. It also looks better visually!

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/84bb9c8b6748470f168f551c13a410d5698f3e1e.png[/img]

[h2]1.2 part 2?[/h2]
Because of engine issues, the second half of 1.2, which will bring full controller & Steam Deck support, is going to be launched within the next half-week or so. Everything is ready, but we are currently just waiting on a hotfix for the engine. Thanks for being patient with us!

If you have anything to say about this update, good or bad, please provide feedback on our discord server or the Steam forums! Thank you so much!

[i]-Encabulated Games[/i]

notes.title: Sunday Devlog 25: Ready for Launch
notes.content:
Finally. After over two long months of chipping away, hair pulling, brain melting, question asking, poll running and even a demo feature catchup, finally, update 1.2 is ready for open bet-

[i]W-what?[/i] The exported game doesn't detect controllers???

...

[h2][b]GOD F-[/b][/h2]

[h1]🚀 Sunday Devlog 25: Ready For Launch[/h1]
Yo! Welcome to the last dev log that'll be discussing 1.2. After a very long and overstretched journey, 1.2 and all the goodies it comes with will be coming to the game on Steam... as soon as a bug with game exporting is fixed :P. Let's talk about what's happened this week!

[h2]Full Controller Gameplay[/h2]

Every single issue and edge-case I've found so far has been patched up, allowing the game to fully support controller inputs! Here are some short gifs of me, with nothing but a controller:

[b]-Navigating between levels[/b]

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/1d3d034fd4c09af83484d9b4e9a9912a7bb0f39b.gif[/img]


[b]-Adjusting the game options[/b]

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/50d27175124b3c4b720e3f6ff595e11ddf6f7724.gif[/img]

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/acfc94610ae512a4e10b111455e1ef737d23431e.gif[/img]

To be honest, the game doesn't feel as fluid on a controller compared to a mouse, but you can get the hang of it after a while. To me, it feels a lot like how it felt to try the game's hard levels for the first time. It is difficult, but doable.

The main objective for this feature was kind of two-fold - implementing controller support, but also support for the Steam deck, which has been steadily increasing in popularity. Multiple people on the Encabulated Games team own Steam decks, so it was always something I was curious about implementing support for.

[h2]New Startup Screen[/h2]

The startup screen gets you into the game a lot quicker, and looks a lot nicer. As opposed to two scenes before the main menu, there is now only one. Also, for some reason, it fills me with a feeling when I see the "Encabulated Games" logo surrounded in animated orange, fully filling my computer screen. Maybe I just like the colors, lol.

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/84bb9c8b6748470f168f551c13a410d5698f3e1e.png[/img]

[h2]Other Smaller Things[/h2]

While the adaptive music for all of the different albums is still underway, I decided to at least implement the adaptive music for the hyper-internet map. Transitioning the two themes was a breeze, and it sounds nice in-game. Thanks BoxLion for the music!

The controller menu is also now done - I touched it up a bit with a header and a button to disable joysticks incase you intend to move the parser across the screen with a touchpad or some other way.

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/6b8c9cb37b22cd9cefca306c5f80d9749379133a.png[/img]

[h2]Splitting The Update?[/h2]

Unfortunately, maintenance on the engine is away for the next week, so if it's for sure an exporter issue, 1.2 with the controller support won't be able to release.

[b]However[/b], 1.2 still comes with a new galaxy map, better key assignments & customization, bug fixes and other fun doodads. Since the Steam Autumn Sale is rapidly approaching, and we do plan on putting the game on sale, [b]the update might be "half-released" without the controller support instead.[/b] Then, once the exported game works with controllers, we can do an open beta for it.

All that aside, thank you for reading through these devlogs as the game's journey continues. My final projects for my college classes are coming up soon, so work on 1.3 will likely begin next week at the earliest. If you are American, enjoy your Thanksgiving. Thanks for reading :).

[i]-Encabulated Games[/i]

notes.title: Sunday Devlog 24: Nearly There
notes.content:
[h1]🤏 Sunday Devlog 24: Nearly There[/h1]
Welcome back! I really did think I would get controller support ready for a 1.2 public beta by now. Let's discuss what happened!

[h2]Controller Menu Navigation Pt.5 billion[/h2]

Last devlog, I was super excited to have the "majority of the challenges" out of the way for 1.2. Unfortunately, this week I realized that there is, in fact, more work to be done.

The main thing is that the detectable "hitboxes" for the buttons in the controller navigation are objects that are separate from the buttons themselves [i](for a variety of reasons)[/i], and on top of that, the object that "finds" these hitboxes needs to account for moving buttons, overlapping UI, and pieces of the UI on separate planes of existence [i](game layers)[/i].

This can be better illustrated using this gif - notice how the button hitboxes appear and vanish depending on if they're supposed to be detected.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057857/d982c3acf31d7136403508e634ebb688c0418bc6.gif[/img]

On top of that, there are a bunch of weird edge cases for hitboxes needing to be displayed or not, buttons reading what the hitbox objects tell them in an unintended way [i](notice how the buttons in the homescreen all bump a little when the options menu is opened)[/i] and a couple more headaches.

Thankfully, someone in the Flowlab community by the name of TheBrickccentric, someone who is an absolute wizard with the engine [i](made a doom-like game and a 3D engine inside a 2D engine)[/i], helped me with some of the more tricky parts of getting this all to work. It's thanks to him that I can, albeit with my brain burning, finish the rest of this update "on my own".

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/233f7808e63154cf0d2df6907465885eb4b18271.png[/img]
[i]Thank you!!![/i]

[h2]Adaptive music[/h2]

ThatBoxLion and Prism4ticTurtle continue to get the adaptive music done for the stage navigation, meanwhile! I can't really embed a playable mp3 into this announcement, but they are roughly 40% done with all of the pieces. We still aren't sure if it'll be done by 1.2, but if not, it will arrive in 1.3, a much less overhaul-y update compared to this one.

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/147308927933d99a0b56b88e3051cdab513dd8ca.png[/img]
[i]You can't hear images, but if it's in BeepBox it's always a banger.[/i]

[h2]1.2??????[/h2]

It may sound weird that I'm going to say this, but the 1.2 steam deck/controller beta is coming this week before the weekend! I was planning on having it ready by today, but there was just too much controller nav work to chug through. After that, though, there really isn't much of anything in the way of a 1.2 steam deck/controller public beta.

Thanks for following the devlog as always, and here's to 1.2 being nearly done!

[i]-Encabulated Games[/i]

notes.title: Sunday Devlog 23: Beep Boopin'
notes.content:
[h1]🔀 Sunday Devlog 23: Beep Boopin'[/h1]
Hey, welcome back! The week prior to this one was very intense and dense, but fortunately this one was less so. Thanks for forgiving us for not putting out a devlog last week. Let's cover what's been going on!

[h2]Controller Menu Navigation[/h2]

Well, I can't hide from the demons anymore.. [b]because the demons are dead![/b] Thanks to the help of Kb-Lemon and Rezarg on the discord for the game engine the game uses [i](Flowlab)[/i], controller menu navigation has been implemented [i](after lots of fried brains including mine)[/i].

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/b47a00c9a1ee75c93851cd1125deffea4cb78ce2.gif[/img]
*These purple squares are temporary, don't worry!*

I completely underestimated how hard it would be to do controller navigation, but now, finally, all of the hard parts have been accounted for. In a nutshell, the controller menu navigation spawns these [i](soon to be)[/i] invisible "target" objects that are paired with their respective buttons, and the game also spawns an object to find those target objects. Pressing the D-pad/joysticks aims the finder object, which finds a target object and then "selects" it. There's a lot more to it than just that, but that's the most simple way I can describe it.

Something I've thought to myself: Has this been worth it? Well, honestly, from a sales standpoint, not really - there are way more desktop than Steam deck users on Steam. That being said, this has been a very fun challenge to make, and to me, that's worth all of the brain cooking and hair pulling. The nav system is still hyper-janky and has kinks to work out, but rest assured they'll be patched before release of 1.2.

[h2]1.2 When?[/h2]

With all of the major things for this update done, the only things left to do are to wrap all the features together and also implement the adaptive menu music. The adaptive music is still being worked on by BoxLion and PrismaticTurtle, but progress is going steady. We'll see if there'll be a beta test of 1.2 before next week!

Thanks for following these dev logs as always! It's super exciting to be almost done with 1.2. We can't wait to present it!!

[i]-Encabulated Games[/i]

notes.title: Sunday Devlog 22: Closing In
notes.content:
[h1]🎯 Sunday Devlog 22: Closing In[/h1]
Yo! We have a surprising amount to cover in this dev log, so let's get right to it!

[h2]Improved Album Deco[/h2]

[b]The deco update has now come to the individual albums![/b] I wanted to make something that both added personality to the albums without being too distracting. I ended up settling on scrolling background elements, and I think they do a lot to help enhance the feel of an album! Here are some of them:

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/a71b287412159e4fbdfdd3590583ec208dacf610.gif[/img]
[i]Bonus points if you recognize the logo in Rift![/i]

With this improvement, the visual overhauls are largely done with this update. The galaxy map and all the deco has taken a while, but I do think it has been worth it. The game feels a lot less like a "music list" and a little more like an adventure! I was originally a little idea-numb when "galaxy map" won the popular vote for a level select overhaul, but I'm very, very glad it did in hindsight [i](even if it made this update take way longer lmao)[/i].

[h2]Controller Menu Progress[/h2]

Some more progress has been made with the controller menu - there are now [b]options to swap the slash types[/b] for the buttons you'd use for slashing!

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/66880ea060d217437580aaffa7f592025f1f017a.gif[/img]

Just a disclaimer: [b]You won't be able to fully rebind everything[/b], so you won't be able to, say, make X restart a level, or make the start button trigger a positive slash. 

This is mainly to help the update go faster and because very little people would want any more customization than swapping the slash types [i](except for joystick inversion.. that may be added too)[/i]. If popular demand requests that more robust button mapping should be added, it will in a future update, however.

With that said, there is more you can now remap on the other type of controller:

[h2]Upgraded Keybindings Screen[/h2]

The keybinding screen has been upgraded in two ways: first, [b]you can now bind restarting and exiting a file![/b] The buttons to do these were a little strange, and I must say that they did disrupt game flow, so the defaults have been adjusted slightly, and you can now adjust them yourself. Enjoy!

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/b74e1bdb8a8e874378a25cbdaf5d6467a498ef8f.gif[/img]

You may also notice that [b]you can bind more keys[/b] now, too! Support for mapping Tab, Caps, Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Backspace, Esc & Enter have all been added. 

Why you would ever want to bind Esc to positive slashing or Caps for restarting a file is beyond me, but it ended up arriving due to needing to rebind Backspace, and it was extremely easy to add binding support for the other non-alphabetical/numerical keys.


[h2]Other News[/h2]

Lastly, a more robust audio system is being developed for the engine. This means that [b]Pausing[/b] and [b]Level Editors[/b] are guaranteed for updates [b]1.3[/b] and [b]2.0[/b], respectively! This is big news to the team, because the engine development is external to us and we don't control it. We wish god speed to Grazer, the developer of the game's engine.

Anyway, thanks for following the development as always. I dunno if next dev log will have as much stuff since a lot of projects for my classes are closing in, but it's been really fun adding all of this stuff and I hope we can get controller menu navigation up and running soon. Until next time!

[i]-Encabulated Games[/i]

Welcome back! Adding controller support continues to be a big job, so let's talk about how that's been going in this devlog!

The controller monitor is now done, showcasing all the controller inputs the player can use!

[h2]Controller Testing[/h2]

The footage doesn't look any different from normal gameplay so it wouldn't make sense to send, but playing the actual game with the controller was tested, and it turns out that moving side to side with the joystick is hard!!

It definitely takes time to get used to, but man.. it feels like I'm brand new to the game trying to use it, lol.

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/f2f9929b6696204dfaa1cd1149839148fe450447.png[/img]
[i]Oof.[/i]

[h2]Getting there..[/h2]

I certainly didn't expect 1.2 to take this long to do, but here we are over a month and a half into its development. Despite how grim it may sound, the one hour per day rule is still going strong! At this rate, I predict that the controller beta will [i]really[/i] go up in 2-3 weeks from now, and that'll last about a week before the 1.2 release. It may come earlier though, we'll have to see.

Working on this game has been a lot of fun and I can't wait to share even more stuff next devlog. Thanks for tuning :)

[h1]💻 Sunday Devlog 20: Steady Progress[/h1]
Hi again! This is gonna be another mini-devlog, but I'm still pretty proud to show stuff off today.

Last week, I took on the task of working on the game one hour per day minimum. I managed to reach this goal, but I realized that my usual weekend turbo-bursts last a little longer than 7 hours, or one hour per day, lol. 

[h2]UI Updates & Controller Monitor[/h2]
The settings menu UI got updated this week to have a bit more personality, including a little EnryoSoft logo in the bottom corner and some snazzy icons next to titles. You'd be surprised by how much a little icon can help wrap up a UI layout in a neat package.
 
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45057857/b0b89b4f2dbd8ddc8aa82c0a1dcbbae911250590.png[/img]

I got hit with a light sickness earlier this weekend, but all it really did was make me feel a little tired. Thanks for following the devlog as always! 20 devlogs ago I decided to start these weekly logs to keep me and the team on track and it has definitely paid off. Here's to another 20!

[i]-Encabulated Games[/i]

notes.title: Monday Devlog 17: Makin' Maps
notes.content:
[h1]📍 Monday Devlog 17: Makin' Maps[/h1]
Welcome back! This week has been busy for me, but I still managed to get a bit done. This will be a short log, but let's talk about some things anyway.

[h2]New "Hyper-Internet" map[/h2]

Something I didn't expect when making the new "galaxy map" [i](now called the hyper-internet)[/i] is just how much work it took to reconfigure the zone select. There are a lot of cool animations and details I'd rather keep secret for now, but just know that navigating through the files is going to feel quite different in version 1.2. Tuning all the numbers and code to fit this map in involved adding a lot of number lists, overrides and other jank.
